# Affine Numerators and Boolean Projection Relations

## Statement

Let $R=\mathbb R[u_1,\ldots,u_n]$, and let $e_0,e_1,\ldots,e_n$ denote the standard basis of $R^{n+1}$. Define the submodule

$$ K=\left\lbrace Q=(Q_0,\ldots,Q_n):Q_0(tx)+\sum_{i=1}^n x_iQ_i(tx)=0\text{ for all }t\in\mathbb R,\ x\in\lbrace0,1\rbrace^n\right\rbrace. $$

**Theorem 1.** The module $K$ is generated by the following linear vectors:

$$ A_i=u_i(e_0-e_i),\qquad B_{ij}=u_i e_j-u_j e_i\quad(1\leq i\lt j\leq n). $$

For positive degree $k$, the homogeneous degree $k$ part of $R^{n+1}/K$ has dimension

$$ \sum_{s=1}^{\min(k+1,n)}\binom ns. $$

Its degree-zero part has dimension $n+1$. In particular, the affine-numerator relation module has linear generators even though the constant-numerator ideal has cubic generators.

## Proof by an explicit normal form

Every displayed generator evaluates to zero: $u_i(e_0-e_i)$ gives $tx_i(1-x_i)$, and $u_ie_j-u_je_i$ gives $t(x_ix_j-x_jx_i)$. Let $L$ be their generated submodule. Thus $L\subseteq K$.

The module $K$ is graded. Indeed, substituting $tx$ into a vector with homogeneous coefficient parts gives a polynomial in $t$, and all its coefficients must vanish separately. In degree zero the tests $x=0,e_1,\ldots,e_n$ force every component to vanish.

Consider a tagged monomial $u^\alpha e_j$ of positive degree $k=|\alpha|$. If $j=0$, choose $i$ with $\alpha_i\gt0$ and use $u_ie_0\equiv u_ie_i$ modulo $L$. Hence it suffices to take $j\neq0$. Let $T=\mathrm{supp}(\alpha)\cup\lbrace j\rbrace$ and $r=\max T$. If $j\neq r$, then $\alpha_r\gt0$, and the relation $u_re_j\equiv u_je_r$ moves the tag to $r$. Every other member of $T$ still occurs as a coefficient variable.

For distinct $i,r$, the generators give the quadratic transfer

$$ u_i^2e_r-u_iu_re_r=u_iB_{ir}-u_rA_i+u_iA_r, $$

where $B_{ir}=u_ie_r-u_re_i$ also for reversed index order. Whenever the coefficient exponent at $i\neq r$ is at least two, multiply this identity by the remaining monomial to transfer one exponent from $i$ to $r$. This terminates, since the sum of excess exponents away from $r$ decreases. The result is

$$ M_{T,k}=u_r^{k-|T|+1}\prod_{i\in T\setminus\lbrace r\rbrace}u_i e_r,\qquad \varnothing\neq T\subseteq[n],\quad |T|\leq k+1. $$

All exponents are nonnegative. Evaluation of $M_{T,k}$ at the Boolean line $tx$, including the tagged coordinate in the evaluation, is $t^k\prod_{i\in T}x_i$. Thus a linear combination of these normal forms that belongs to $K$ has coefficients $c_T$ satisfying

$$ \sum_{\varnothing\neq T\subseteq U}c_T=0\qquad(\varnothing\neq U\subseteq[n],\ |U|\leq k+1). $$

Induction on $|U|$ makes every coefficient zero. Consequently the normal forms are independent modulo $K$, and any homogeneous member of $K$ reduces to zero modulo $L$. This proves $K=L$ and both dimension formulas. The proof is an explicit terminating reduction, with at most $3k+2$ monomial multiples of the stated generators per input tagged monomial of degree $k$. $\blacksquare$

## Classification of affine-residue reciprocal deformations

Let $a_{v,i}\in\mathbb R$ have finite support in $v\in\mathbb N^n$, and let

$$ P_i(z)=\sum_v a_{v,i}z^v,\qquad Q_i(u)=P_i(1+u),\qquad D(x)=1+b\cdot x,\quad b_i\gt0. $$

**Theorem 2.** The identity

$$ \sum_v\frac{a_{v,0}+\sum_i a_{v,i}x_i}{D(x)+\varepsilon v\cdot x}=0 $$

holds for every Boolean $x$ and every nonnegative $\varepsilon$ if and only if $Q\in K$.

**Proof.** For fixed $x$, group terms by $m=v\cdot x$. The positive values of $m$ give distinct poles at $-D(x)/m$. Vanishing on an interval is equivalent to a zero rational function, so its residues and then its constant term force each group sum to vanish. Conversely those zero group sums imply the identity. Equivalently the polynomial

$$ P_0(t^{x_1},\ldots,t^{x_n})+\sum_i x_iP_i(t^{x_1},\ldots,t^{x_n}) $$

vanishes identically in $t$. Since $t^{x_i}=1+(t-1)x_i$, this is exactly membership of $Q$ in $K$. $\blacksquare$

Translation of the generators gives two local identities, valid for Boolean $x_i,x_j$:

$$ (1-x_i)\left(\frac1{D+\varepsilon x_i}-\frac1D\right)=0, $$

$$ x_j\left(\frac1{D+\varepsilon x_i}-\frac1D\right)-x_i\left(\frac1{D+\varepsilon x_j}-\frac1D\right)=0. $$

Multiplication by a monomial in $z$ translates every denominator velocity by the same nonnegative integer vector. Theorem 1 therefore proves that every identity in Theorem 2 is a finite real linear combination of translates of these two-head and three-head identities. There is no uniform bound here in terms of the original head count: expanding between $z$ and $z-1$ can increase the support, and velocity magnitudes are unrestricted.

## Graph circulations give minimal identities in growing dimension

Let $G$ be a finite simple graph on $[n]$, with one orientation chosen for each edge. For an oriented edge $i\to j$, use the two velocity vectors $2e_i+e_j$ and $e_i+2e_j$. Give their reciprocal heads constant residues $a_{ij}$ and $b_{ij}$ respectively, and use the common positive base $D(x)$ from Theorem 2.

**Theorem 3.** This family is identically zero on the Boolean cube for all nonnegative $\varepsilon$ if and only if

$$ b_{ij}=-a_{ij}\quad\text{for every edge},\qquad \sum_{i\to j}a_{ij}-\sum_{j\to i}a_{ji}=0\quad\text{at every vertex }i. $$

Thus its space of identities is the real circulation space of the graph.

**Proof.** The projection test $x=e_i+e_j$ isolates the two heads on edge $\lbrace i,j\rbrace$ in the group $v\cdot x=3$. Simplicity of the graph ensures that every other edge gives projection at most two. The group coefficient must vanish, proving $a_{ij}+b_{ij}=0$.

Next $x=e_i$ and the group with projection two give precisely the displayed divergence equation. Conversely, after antisymmetry is imposed, an edge with equal input bits contributes zero. An edge crossing the cut contributes its signed flow times the common scalar

$$ \frac1{D(x)+2\varepsilon}-\frac1{D(x)+\varepsilon}. $$

The sum of signed flows across any cut is the sum of the divergences inside it, hence zero. This proves sufficiency. $\blacksquare$

For a directed cycle on $n\geq3$ vertices, all edge flows must be equal. Therefore its $2n$ reciprocal families have a unique relation up to scale, with every coefficient nonzero. Every proper subfamily is independent as functions of both $x$ and $\varepsilon$. Their velocity configuration has affine dimension $n-1$: all vectors have coordinate sum three, and the differences within the edge pairs are $e_i-e_{i+1}$, which span the zero-sum hyperplane.

This minimality is for the entire deformation family. It is not a claim of linear independence after fixing one value of $\varepsilon$.

## High contact without a persistent subidentity

**Theorem 4.** For every integer $m\geq3$, there are $H=m+5$ distinct nonnegative velocity vectors in three dimensions, with full affine span and nonzero constant residues, whose Boolean reciprocal sum has exact contact order $m$ at a common-denominator collision. Their moment columns through order $m-1$ form a circuit, but the reciprocal families themselves have no nonzero persistent linear relation.

**Proof.** Start with the line velocities $v_h=(2+4h)(1,1,1)$ for $0\leq h\leq m$ and coefficients $c_h=(-1)^{m-h}\binom mh$. Expanding $\sum_{h=0}^m c_h e^{ht}=(e^t-1)^m$ shows that the weighted powers of $h$ vanish below degree $m$ and that the degree $m$ weighted power is $m!$. Replace the point $v_0$ by the five points

$$ w_A=(3,3,2),\quad w_B=(2,4,2),\quad w_C=(3,2,2),\quad w_D=(1,4,2),\quad w_E=(1,3,2), $$

with residue vector $c_0(-1,1,1,-1,1)$. The translated six-point switch gives an identity of whole Boolean reciprocal families:

$$ \frac1{D+\varepsilon v_0\cdot x}=-\frac1{D+\varepsilon w_A\cdot x}+\frac1{D+\varepsilon w_B\cdot x}+\frac1{D+\varepsilon w_C\cdot x}-\frac1{D+\varepsilon w_D\cdot x}+\frac1{D+\varepsilon w_E\cdot x}. $$

Consequently the replacement does not change the score. Its Taylor moments of order less than $m$ vanish on the cube. At $x=e_3$, the degree $m$ moment equals $\sum_h c_h(2+4h)^m=4^m m!\neq0$, so the contact order is exactly $m$. Use $D(x)=1+x_1+x_2+x_3$; every denominator has strictly positive coherent slopes for $\varepsilon\geq0$.

We prove the circuit assertion explicitly. Suppose coefficients $d_h$ on the retained line points and $s_A,\ldots,s_E$ on the five new points annihilate all Boolean moments through degree $m-1$. The test $x=e_3$ groups the five new points at projection two, with the remaining distinct projections $2+4h$ for $1\leq h\leq m$. The $m$ by $m+1$ Vandermonde matrix has a one-dimensional kernel. Thus for some $\lambda$,

$$ d_h=\lambda c_h,\qquad s_A+s_B+s_C+s_D+s_E=\lambda c_0. $$

Subtract the $e_3$ tests from the $e_1$ tests in degrees one and two. The line contributions cancel. The remaining offsets are $1,0,1,-1,-1$, so the two equations force $s_A+s_C=0$ and $s_D+s_E=0$. Subtracting the $e_3$ tests from the $e_2$ tests similarly uses offsets $1,2,0,2,1$ and gives $s_A+s_E=0$ and $s_B+s_D=0$. These four equations force

$$ (s_A,s_B,s_C,s_D,s_E)=\lambda c_0(-1,1,1,-1,1). $$

Therefore the full truncated-moment kernel has dimension one, and its generator has no zero coefficient. Every proper subfamily of moment columns is independent.

Any persistent reciprocal identity would satisfy these truncated moments and hence be a scalar multiple of this vector. Its nonzero degree $m$ moment forces that scalar to be zero. Finally $w_A-w_C=(0,1,0)$ and $w_B-w_D=(1,0,0)$ span the first two coordinate directions, while $v_1$ has third coordinate six and every new point has third coordinate two. The affine span is all three-dimensional space. $\blacksquare$

This circuit property concerns the concatenated moment tests, and independence of reciprocal families means functions of both the input and the deformation parameter. Neither statement asserts independence of the tables at a fixed parameter value. The construction also has an economical equivalent collinear representation before the substitution; it is not a Boolean head-complexity lower bound.

## A precise obstruction to a Schur-product transfer

[Li and Liu, Theorem 1.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2606.24349v1), prove that a circuit of $t$ formal $m$-th powers of linear forms whose underlying span has dimension $r$ satisfies $t\geq m(r-1)+2$. Their proof uses a Schur-product growth theorem. Its circuit hypothesis concerns formal polynomials, not Boolean evaluations.

The directed-cycle construction shows why minimality alone does not repair this distinction. Set

$$ \ell_i^+=z_0+2z_i+z_{i+1},\qquad \ell_i^-=z_0+z_i+2z_{i+1},\qquad i\in\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z. $$

These linear forms span a space of dimension $n$. Their squares form a formal circuit: a quadratic relation forces opposite coefficients on each edge by looking at $z_iz_{i+1}$, and then equal flows around the cycle by looking at $z_i^2$. The all-equal flow is indeed a relation, by telescoping. This attains the bound $2n=2(n-1)+2$.

In contrast, their formal cubes are linearly independent. For each edge, the coefficients of $z_i^2z_{i+1}$ and $z_iz_{i+1}^2$ give the invertible two-by-two system with rows $(12,6)$ and $(6,12)$. No other edge supplies these monomials, even when $n=3$.

Nevertheless, for every nonnegative integer $m$ and every Boolean $x$,

$$ \sum_i\left((1+2x_i+x_{i+1})^m-(1+x_i+2x_{i+1})^m\right)=0. $$

If the bits agree the summand vanishes; if they differ it equals $(3^m-2^m)(x_i-x_{i+1})$, and the sum telescopes. Thus a relation that is minimal throughout the reciprocal deformation does not supply a formal power relation even in degree three. A Schur-growth argument for the full model would need a new multiplication-compatible space that retains Boolean evaluation, rather than importing the formal-power theorem unchanged.

## Verification and scope

The four general theorems have complete written proofs above. An exact-arithmetic replay checks the tagged-monomial transfers and quotient dimensions, and independently checks graph projection kernels, cycle ranks, and the high-contact circuit ranks. The companion Lean file checks the local scalar identities, the module transfer equation, and the cycle identity for every permutation of any finite type and every real function of the projected velocity. It does not formalize the complete polynomial-module classification or the arbitrary-graph circuit theorem.

All reciprocal families here have affine numerators, strictly positive coherent slopes, and unrestricted signed residues. This resolves the affine-numerator gap for the stated integer-velocity deformation classification. It does not classify arbitrary real velocities, multiple collision scales, or representations at a single target-dependent parameter point. No unrestricted classification-chamber count or asymptotic head lower bound has been obtained.
